Variable dictionary of the input data

Source: R/data.R
variable_dictionary.Rd

The input variables the OECD Scale Up project asks for, one row per variable of each input file: the firm-level panel base_financials, the optional establishment file plants_RAW and, for the trade package, the transaction-level trade_RAW. It carries the OECD variable dictionary (definitions, formats, codings, sources, priorities and notes) and adds what this package does with each variable. vignette("input-data") and vignette("input-trade-data") are built from it.

Usage

variable_dictionary

Format

A data frame with one row per dataset and variable:

dataset

"base_financials", "plants_RAW" or "trade_RAW".

file

File name the pipeline reads from input_dir; <CT> is the two-letter country code of config_scaleup().

variable

Variable name, as the pipeline expects it.

definition

What the variable measures.

format

"numeric" or "string".

coding

Values of an indicator or code variable.

source

Usual statistical source: BR (business register), BD (business demography), SBS (structural business statistics), ITGS / ITSS (international trade in goods / services statistics), IFATS (inward foreign affiliates statistics), EuroGroups register.

sbs_code

SBS variable code, where there is one.

priority

The OECD request: "must-have", "nice-to-have, first order" or "nice-to-have, second order".

notes

Further notes of the OECD dictionary.

package_requirement

What the package needs: "required" (the build stops without it), "required unless age_cat is supplied", "required (if the file is supplied)", "optional" (used when present) or "not used".

package_use

What the package does with the variable.

money

TRUE for money variables, expected in EUR thousand and divided by 1000 when financials_unit = "EUR" (for trade_value: trade_value_unit = "EUR").

negatives_missing

TRUE if the build sets negative values to missing.

Source

OECD Scale Up project variable dictionary (Phase 3); the package columns from this package's code. Built by data-raw/variable_dictionary.R.
